program.name: Swift Agent — Realtime Cloud Delivery
program.description: Make the locally working realtime runtime accessible, reliable, and verifiable through deployed AWS environments: unify REST + WebSocket onto a single public port, establish one canonical WebSocket URL contract, wire PUBLIC_WEBSOCKET_URL through Terraform/SSM/ECS with fail-fast validation, harden deploy-time connection draining, correct Redis fanout and health, align the React SDK and site docs, and add a deployed realtime smoke test that blocks releases.

successCriteria.description: REST and WebSocket are served on a single public port (3000); /v1/stream is reachable through the existing ALB with no separate gateway port exposed in the container, task definition, or security group.
Session creation returns, and the SDK consumes, one canonical WebSocket URL of the form wss://<host>/v1/stream?token=<jwt>.
PUBLIC_WEBSOCKET_URL is provisioned via Terraform/SSM and injected into ECS with correct per-environment (dev/staging/prod) wss:// values.
Startup fails fast when PUBLIC_WEBSOCKET_URL is missing or localhost in a cloud environment — the silent ws://localhost:3001 fallback is removed.
Graceful shutdown drains in-flight WebSocket connections within the configured ECS stop window, and ALB idle-timeout/stickiness/deregistration are tuned for long-lived sockets.
Redis fanout delivers run events to locally-connected sockets on the subscribing instance, and /health reports Redis reachability via PING.
The single-task posture, process-local replay-buffer and session-lock limits, and in-flight-run/reconnect-replay behavior are documented.
The React/vanilla SDK consumes the API-provided canonical URL using safe URL construction; the redundant sessionId query parameter and the double-? construction bug are removed.
Site docs and the quickstart document the canonical /v1/stream endpoint and are validated against deployed dev.
A deployed WebSocket smoke test exercises session create → connect → auth → event stream, and its failure blocks the deploy in dev, staging, and production.
Staging/production Docker build inconsistencies are resolved so all environments build and deploy from an identical image path.
Monorepo type-checking, linting, unit tests, and integration tests pass.

successCriteriaNotes: The runtime loop, gateway protocol, Redis pub/sub adapters, and AWS Terraform stacks already exist (see docs/as-built.md). This program exposes, configures, drains, and verifies the gateway; it does not change the runtime loop, stream event protocol, or trace schema. Key decisions: unify REST + WebSocket onto port 3000 (no new ALB target group/listener rule) and pin a single gateway task for the MVP (horizontal scale deferred to Phase 2).

workstreams.name: Realtime Infra: Single-Port Routing & Drain Tuning

runtimeEndpoints.purpose: Authenticated bidirectional WebSocket stream, now served on the unified public port (3000) and reachable through the ALB via the canonical wss://<host>/v1/stream?token=<jwt> contract

architectureDecisions.decision: Unify REST and WebSocket onto a single public port (3000)
architectureDecisions.rationale: The ALB already forwards /v1/stream to 3000; mounting the gateway as a plugin on the API Fastify app avoids a new target group, listener rule, security-group port, and second health check. Smallest infra surface for a single-task MVP.
alternativesRejected: Path-route /v1/stream to a separate port-3001 target group (more infra)
Separate rt.* hostname with host-based routing (DNS/ACM SAN + most infra)

architectureDecisions.decision: Pin a single gateway task for the realtime MVP
architectureDecisions.rationale: Verify Redis fanout correctness and add a Redis health check, but keep desired count = 1 and document the process-local replay-buffer/session-lock limits. Avoids cross-instance lock/replay complexity.
alternativesRejected: Support horizontal scale now (cross-instance A→B streaming, multi-instance CI test) — deferred to Phase 2 durable layer

outOfScope: Horizontal multi-instance realtime scaling (cross-instance replay/lock semantics) — Phase 2
A separate rt.* realtime hostname or CloudFront fronting
A second ALB target group / listener rule (obviated by the single-port decision)
Durable/persisted replay buffer and shared session lock across instances
Changes to the runtime loop, providers, executor resolution, or stream event protocol
New trace/span schema or metrics work (covered by persist-observe)
